original_test_intent: Verify the intended BMC WebUI account/session can be logged out and reaches an unambiguously unauthenticated page without unintended impact on required automation or recovery channels.
original_method: At the owner-approved final sequence point, an authorized operator verifies the exact dedicated browser session, clicks Log out, captures the unauthenticated confirmation, checks protected-page access is denied and confirms independent re-login/recovery remains available.
manual_activity: An authorized operator must click Log out and visually confirm the browser's unauthenticated state; the agent cannot attest the local browser transition from SSH/API telemetry.
required_inputs: Exact BMC/SUT, account and browser-session identity
Confirmation the session is dedicated and which automation/API sessions must survive
Owner-approved final sequencing after pending Web actions/downloads
Expected logged-out page/redirect and protected-page denial behavior
Independent re-login/recovery path and session-impact observer
safety_requirements: Perform only at the approved final point with no unsaved work
Do not clear cookies globally, reset all sessions, change credentials or alter BMC settings
Never capture tokens/passwords in screenshots or logs
Stop on wrong account, shared-session dependency or lost recovery access
Do not automatically repeat logout or test broad session revocation
agent_execution_scope: Verify sequencing and non-secret session context
Package redacted operator evidence and optional session-impact observations
Confirm provided evidence shows protected-page denial and independent recovery
Make no browser-action claim, retry or PASS/FAIL verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target session/final sequence and recovery path
Review intended versus unintended session impact and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No SSH/IPMI command can prove the local browser's authenticated session ended; DeepSeek's NO assessment is correct, though logging out one Web session should not inherently terminate independent IPMI/Redfish sessions unless they share credentials/session context.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use browser/operator evidence for the exact session. Optional non-secret API monitoring may observe unintended impact but cannot replace the WebUI logout proof.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Root-label menu, Log out action, account logout criterion and 1/1-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a dedicated session, capture redacted before/after UI, attempt a protected-page navigation without reauthentication, and independently verify recovery/other approved channels after logout.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds final sequencing, denial proof and channel-isolation evidence without broadening into session reset or credential change.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An SSH/API status cannot reveal whether the browser retained a valid cookie, and a login-page screenshot alone may result from navigation rather than actual session invalidation; protected-resource denial closes that gap.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Browser caches can display stale content; acceptance must use an authenticated protected request/navigation and avoid exposing response tokens.

project_override_considerations: If project policy intentionally invalidates all Web sessions, that broader effect requires explicit approval and its own recovery evidence; it must not be inferred from this single-session source.
expected_evidence: Verified BMC/account/dedicated-session identity and approved final sequencing
Redacted pre-logout page and operator action timestamp
Logged-out page/redirect plus protected-page denial in the same session
Independent re-login/recovery and unintended-channel impact result
No token/credential/config change/no-auto-retry audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require WebUI logout. DeepSeek and GPT agree the defining evidence is browser/operator state.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The agent cannot execute/observe the local browser action, but an authorized operator can; MANUAL ONLY is correct.

review_improvement: Preserves logout scope while requiring protected-resource denial and session isolation, preventing a login-page screenshot or unrelated API status from being mistaken for success.
independent_technical_reasoning: Logout must invalidate the intended browser credential, not merely navigate away from a protected page. A cached login page proves little, so the same session should be denied when reopening a protected resource. At the same time, terminating unrelated recovery or automation channels would be an unintended blast radius; using a dedicated session and sequencing the case last separates these outcomes.
